newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks shed gains after hitting all-time high.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks shed gains after hitting all-time high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index succumbed to profit-taking on Thursday after handover enthusiasm pushed stocks to an all-time high in early trade.
The index was down 154 points, or 1.02 percent, at 15,041 after surging to an early record high of 15,363.61 points.
Property stocks led the market down after Hong Kong's new government said on Tuesday it would increase housing supply to deal with escalating real estate prices.
"(Chief executive) Tung Chee-hwa said he will regulate the property market," said one trader on the stock exchange floor.
Major property developers tumbled with Cheung Kong down HK$3.25 at HK$73.25, Henderson Land off HK$2.25 at HK$66.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties down HK$3.50 at HK$89.75.

Meanwhile, red chip stocks retained a firm tone although they were also off their early highs. The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index was up 38 points, or 1.10 percent, at 3,507 after hitting an early high of 3561.23 points.
The Hong Kong stock market was closed on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday to celebrate Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30.
Today is the first trading day under Chinese rule.
"Handover fever is coming to an end and investors are taking a break in the short run before taking new positions," said Edwin Cheung, a senior sales manager at Taiwan Securities.
"Profit-taking is a bit hectic but we expect support at the 15,000 level," he added.
Turnover was a hefty HK$4.47 billion after the first half hour of trade.
Banking stocks made hefty gains with HSBC Holdings jumping to a record high of HK$239.00 before paring its gains to trade up HK$2.00 at HK$235.00.
Hang Seng Bank also hit an all-time high at HK$116.00 before trading up HK$1.00 at HK$111.50.
